title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions and Mixed Numbers, and Fractions of Whole Numbers
seo_title: Grade 5 Fraction Calculations Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Add and subtract common fractions in which one denominator is a multiple of another and mixed numbers (same denominators); solve problems involving common fractions, including grouping and equal sharing; find fractions of whole numbers which result in whole numbers; recognise, describe and use the equivalence of division and fractions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 fraction worksheets: adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers, fractions of whole numbers and division as fractions. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Fraction of a number: ÷ denominator, × numerator.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Fractions with the same denominator: add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.
  • Mixed numbers: add the wholes and the fractions. If the fraction part is 1 or more, regroup it as a whole.
  • Fraction of a whole number: divide by the denominator, multiply by the numerator. 35 of 40: 40 ÷ 5 × 3 = 24.
  • Division and fractions: 3 ÷ 4 = 34.

Examples

Example

2 35 + 1 45

3 + 75

75 = 1 25

Answer: 4 25

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding denominatorsKeep the denominator.
Not regrouping7/5 = 1 2/5.
Dividing by the numeratorDivide by the denominator first.

The bar is split into sixths. The shaded part is 56, and 13 is crossed out. What is 56 − 13?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: 6 is a multiple of 3, so use 6 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 13 = 26. Subtract the numerators: 56 − 26 = 36. Simplify: divide the numerator and denominator of 36 by 3 to get 12. The answer is 12.

items.q: The green part is 14 and the yellow part is 38. The dashed lines split the green bar into eighths. How many eighths is the green part?
items.e: Each quarter is split into 2. So 14 = 28: there are 28 in the green part. Now both fractions are in eighths, so you can add or subtract them.

items.q: Write 75 as a mixed number.
items.e: 7 ÷ 5 = 1 remainder 2. So 75 is 1 whole and 25 left over: 1 25.

items.q: Write 114 as a mixed number.

items.q: Write 176 as a mixed number.
items.e: 17 ÷ 6 = 2 remainder 5. So 176 is 2 wholes and 56 left over: 2 56.

items.q:
Palesa spends 34 of an hour on homework and half an hour practising the piano. How long does she spend altogether?
Give your answer as a mixed number.
c: 14 of an hour
23 of an hour
items.e: 4 is a multiple of 2, so use 4 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 12 = 24. Add the numerators: 34 + 24 = 54. 54 is an improper fraction: 54 = 1 14. The answer is 1 14 hours. (That is 1 hour 15 minutes.)

items.q: A tin holds 2 litres of paint. A decorator uses 58 litre. How much paint is left in the tin?
items.e: Exchange 1 whole for 88: 2 = 1 88. Subtract the fractions: 88 − 58 = 38. The whole number left is 1. The answer is 1 38 litres.
